1.Description: Can find food, water and shelter in the wilderness. In practical terms this means that on extended length adventures the player may supply their own provisions, which may be kept in an Out-Of-Character location until foraged for

1.Name: 1st Extra Level of Life
1.Description: Gains 1st extra level of life. This replaces the post-8th tables ability

Amlesian.Description: Select an Amlesian caste to define your standing.

Eta.Description: The lowest of the low. They have no position, no honour, and no regard. It is impossible for one of this caste to rise beyond their starting position. They perform the most menial of tasks.

Peasant.Description: The class of the masses. Many fall within the caste, even those with great talents. It is common, and although all but the Eta are above their station they are important within the social system.

Artisan.Description: From a family of trade or talent the family will have money and some respect. They are rarely skilled in arms or the mystical arts, but they serve a valued role.

Mystical One.Description: A Priest, Wizard or similar. They are respected for their wisdom and power, though seen as less important than warriors in a land dominated by martial talent.

Protector.Description: The warriors of the land. They serve and protect the people and clans. Their duty is to ensure the Empire remains intact and its power strong.

Samurai.Description: The highest standing an individual can start with. They sit beneath the clan heads, and are considered the most honourable within the lands. An individual of Samurai standing is bound by the Code of Jade and if they fail to fulfil it are expected to commit Seppuku. Those seeking to start at the Samurai caste must buy the Honoured One Status unless they are a warrior and have purchased the Samurai tradition. Should an individual rise in social rank they must buy their new caste ability, but any points spent on previous castes reduce the cost of this.

Dishonoured One.Description: These are people who have failed to adhere to the strict caste system of Amles and refused to submit to justice. They may be dishonoured warriors, rebel heroes, or bandits. Those choosing this route must purchase the Dishonoured One Status rather than a caste ability. Dishonoured Ones are all Ostracised within Amles.

Fortune.Description: A servant of the Celestial Realms. An individual choosing this path must purchase the Fortune Status rather than a caste. Fortunes often move through Amles keeping their identities a secret to avoid the Oni that hunt them.

Oni.Description: A creature born from the Shadowlands. They purchase the Oni Status rather than a caste. It is important to note that Oni are hunted within Amles and may be killed on sight.

Rhagrimm.Name: Invoke Ancestor (Rhagrimm)
Rhagrimm.Description: Invoking Duke Rhagrimm grants the descendant +2 resistance levels against magical effects, and 1 point of MAC for every 2 levels possessed (1st to 8th only, not multi-classes). These benefits last 5 minutes.

Issalania.Name: Invoke Ancestor (Issalania)
Issalania.Description: Invoking Issalania allows the descendant to trigger turbulent and opposing emotions in one target within 20'. This is considered a magical and spiritual effect. At the user's choice the target is filled either with love or terror of them, either being Beguiled or struck with Fear at unlimited levels of effect. However, this influence lasts only five minutes, after which time the target is filled with hatred for the user, and gains a 25% rage against them if the target chooses to attack them.

Ulio.Name: Invoke Ancestor (Ulio)
Ulio.Description: Invoking Ulio makes the descendant shimmer and disappear, albeit briefly. For 10 seconds the user becomes entirely invisible to any form of sight. However this invisibility is broken should they strike a blow, cast a spell, or use other innate abilities. The sensations involved in being clouded from men's gaze by Ulio are unpleasant, and the user suffers a -2 dexterity AC penalty for 5 minutes afterwards (cannot reduce dexterity below 0).

Eva.Name: Invoke Ancestor (Eva)
Eva.Description: Invoking Duchess Eva fills the user with potent power, albeit temporarily, this grants them + 1 strength above normal maximums, and + 1 max damage vs. one chosen target. This lasts for a maximum of 1 minute.

1.Name: Disguise
1.Description:
This skill allows the pathfinder to attempt to take on the disguise of a monster or character of a different race.
It costs nothing for the scout to apply the disguise to themselves. It costs 200 grulls to disguise someone else for one adventure, buying them an appropriate card from the Desk before the adventure, or giving the money to the referee. Alternatively, if excellent in-character phys reps in non-20th (or 21st) Century containers are possessed it is free to apply a disguise during Time In on adventure. However, whilst it is possible to disguise your physical appearance you cannot change your smell, size of spirit etc. So a disguise is only as good as a disguise is good.
 If a non-human is to be disguised, they need to apply their normal make up first and then apply the ‘disguise’ over the top of this. Though it might be acceptable for him to be disguised as another non-human with appropriate face paint etc.
 NB you cannot under any circumstances be disguised as another one of your own characters.

5.Name: Conditioned Heartstop
5.Description: If ever reveals information regarding the Buladajn Clan, their heart stops immediately and permanently. This has no immunity.

8.Name: Psi-Scan
8.Description: Tells the user the surface thoughts of one target at time of use. The creature must be within sight.

1.Name: Disarm Traps
1.Description:
Interestingly, there's no official text for this anywhere. Scouts can't do it. You now officially have a skill that does nothing.
Unofficially, your skill lets you disarm traps (though this is at the real-world skill level of the one using the skill)

1.Name: Trap-Wary (8)
1.Description:
May use a Jump innate that requires no verbal to leap out of the area of an area-effect attack, if the Jump has sufficient range to leave the area of effect. If the effect was damaging, only half damage is taken – if non-damaging, it does not affect the user.
and may choose Tomb Robber as a tendency for 0 points rather than normal cost, if the character enters the scout bracket as a second class, they may acquire Tomb Robber tendency on table 9 for 80 points 
Unofficially, you gain this at first level. Levels in it don't change anything.

3.Name: Read Languages
3.Description: This skill allows the Pathfinder to read written languages such as wizardly glyphs, priest runes, elfish high script, dwarfish, etc. To read these runes, however, you must actually be able to read them yourself; the referee will not translate them for you, although use of a crib sheet is acceptable.

1.Description: See through all forms of supernatural darkness

1.Description: For the next 5 minutes, the user is aware whether any statements he hears the target make are lies.

2.Name: Ward Pact (Undead)
2.Description:
An Ancient Folk gains certain ‘pacts’ with other-worldly creatures as they gain levels. These pacts are gained at second, fourth, six and eighth level. They are gained at no cost, and once a player has chosen a level’s pact it may never be changed.
For a pact to work against a specific creature the Ancient Folk must announce their pact clearly within hearing of that creature. They must loudly state their name, ancestry, and what they have a pact with.
If an Ancient Folk betrays a pact, by announcing it and then attacking that creature (except in purest self-defence), that pact is lost forever. The exact effect of a ward pact depends on the relative levels of the Ancient Folk and the creature. Pacts only fully affect creatures of the same or lower level than the user.
Creatures fully affected by an Ancient Folk’s ward pact may not choose to attack the Ancient Folk, except in purest self-defence. They may be forced to do so if controlled by another, such as a controlled undead or elemental, but will be reluctant and attempt to choose other targets where possible. In the situation where an affected creature strikes the Ancient Folk by mistake, it should be considered that at the last minute the creature realised the nature of his target, due to supernatural forces, and pulled back so inflicting no damage.
Creatures of too high a level to be fully affected by a pact will still be aware of the nature of the pact, and will generally act in a friendlier manner towards the Ancient Folk - the exact actions taken dependent on the creature in question. This is only a ‘role-play’ effect, but should usually make a noticeable difference in attitude.
The ward pacts standardly available to Ancient Folk are listed below. It is possible for individuals to seek to forge other pacts, though these are individual and handled with points requests. The exception to this is the Pact with Glass as detailed in the post 8th tables later on. 

• Undead- This works on all forms of undead. 
• Elemental - There are six different pacts, Salamanders, Shades, Sprites, Sylphs, Gnomes, and Undines. Each pact only affects elementals of that element. 
• Supernatural Power - The Ancient Folk may select a specific deity. The pact works against supernatural minions of that deity. If a pact is taken with a Magical Dragon or Drake this does not grant a pact with elves or elementals of that colour. For example, a pact with the Lady of the Stars would not influence priests of the Lady of the Stars, but would affect her angels.
• Elvenkind - May be any one of fire, air, earth, water, light, dark, drowe, winter, twilight or wood elves. 
• Faeries may not be pacted, nor may Seasonal, Onyx or Jade Elves

5.Name: Make and Arm Snap Trap
5.Description:
This skill enables the Hislehasp to make and arm a snap trap which, when set off, inflicts 9 tblp or 3 hits to a monster. If a weapon mastery in snap traps is possessed then it inflicts 15 tblp or 5 hits to a monster. Additionally, for each skill level above 3rd, it inflicts another 3 tblp or 1 Hit. For example, at 4th level skill 12 tblp (or 18 tblp if weapon mastery is taken) would be inflicted. Furthermore, if 6th level skill is possessed, the location of the target that is closest to the triggered trap takes the damage as locational damage as well, stopped only by innate (non-armour) PAC, at 1pt per point of AC. Snap traps cannot be thrown and are ineffective if placed within 1 foot of another trap.
The Pathfinder can make 1 trap for each skill level he possesses in this skill.
When possible, the adventure referee will provide phys reps for these traps if available from the Desk, though the user will often be asked to provide their own.

5.Name: Acute Hearing
5.Description: Allows the user to hear the movements of any creature within 60’. Effectively this means that when the character uses the ability by declaring ‘Acute Hearing’ all creatures within hearing should indicate their broad race category (e.g. elven) and location. At ref’s discretion some creatures may not make sounds, and things walking within walls are generally silent as the walls muffle their noises.

1.Name: Perfect Human disguise
1.Description: May assume a human like appearance as a disguise which may not be penetrated by either physical or mystical means. Once this form is assumed (and the choice to do so must be done at the beginning of the adventure) they look and smell human in all ways, and no method will disprove this concealment. This mystical protection also extends to their choice of name for the adventure, their alignment and their profession. e.g. Hillis the Altunhust Horstval Druid of neutral good alignment takes a human form at the beginning of the adventure. To all means of detection he chooses to be Trewin, the Human Warrior and to appear to be Lawful Neutral in alignment. All spells, miracles and other powers as well as physical training will indicate this is the case. At the start of another adventure he could be completely different.
